title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
source: Aud > cassette x 2 > CD, mics balcony center 15' spread

ai_review.summary: Stunning early‑Dead performance captured on a high‑quality audience tape – Dark Star, Not Fade Away and the Sugar Magnolia jam are legendary.
ai_review.review: Fans hail this June 1970 show as one of the Dead’s all‑time peak performances, repeatedly praising the soaring Dark Star, relentless Not Fade Away chase and the flawless Dark‑Star→Sugar Magnolia transition.  Although it is an audience (AUD) recording, reviewers describe the sound as remarkably clear and immersive – the crowd adds excitement without masking the music.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen enthusiastic 5‑star reviews highlight exceptional musical moments; recording quality is consistently praised as one of the best audience tapes, with only minor complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note crisp instrument separation and a vivid crowd vibe; a few mention occasional imperfections but overall consider it an excellent AUD source for this era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show is lauded for seamless, psychedelic transitions – Dark Star into Sugar Magnolia, multiple Attics segues, and a high‑energy NFA that keeps the momentum flowing throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as perfect, break‑neck speed, and channeling an otherworldly vibe.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work highlighted in the NFA chase and praised for locking in with the rhythm section.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir noted for his outlaw‑cowboy vocal on Me & My Uncle and strong interplay during jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are repeatedly called “locked” and a solid foundation for the improvisations.
